name: view-mode-registry
purpose: Defines selectable repository and platform viewing modes so user, developer, and superadmin development surfaces stay distinct from install and work modes.

reader_guide.summary: Use this registry when choosing what the platform UI or an operator should show. It does not install dependencies and it does not change work close-out strictness.
how_to_read: Read mode_boundary first so view_mode is not confused with install_mode or work_mode.
Use default_mode for current workspace-monitor behavior unless the user explicitly asks for a simpler lens.
Read modes[].visibility_rules to understand which surfaces are foregrounded, collapsed, or hidden.
Treat security_notes as design constraints for future authenticated deployments, not as proof that access control already exists.
update_triggers: A new UI or dashboard role is added.
workspace-monitor changes how documents, operations, agents, or governance records are displayed.
The platform adds real authentication, authorization, or per-user publishing rules.
The distinction between user, developer, and superadmin operator responsibilities changes.
Install mode or work mode rules change in a way that could confuse operators.

structure_rules.rule: view_mode controls what a person or UI sees; install_mode controls dependency and environment setup.
structure_rules.reason: The user/developer installation split already exists and should not be overloaded with UI visibility semantics.

structure_rules.rule: view_mode controls audience lens; work_mode still controls task planning, evidence, evaluation, and close-out strictness.
structure_rules.reason: A superadmin development view must not weaken governance requirements or replace evaluator gates.

structure_rules.rule: The current default view_mode is superadmin_developer because the repository is still being built by the owner and needs governance, agent, history, config, and implementation surfaces visible together.
structure_rules.reason: The latest user request asked for a superadmin-oriented development mode selector for now.

structure_rules.rule: View mode filtering is an operator/UI lens until real authentication and authorization are implemented; do not treat hidden UI elements as a security boundary.
structure_rules.reason: Static repository snapshots can still contain data unless the collector and deployment publication rules enforce removal.

field_guide.meaning: Explains the difference between view_mode, install_mode, and work_mode.
Fallback viewing mode when no explicit UI lens is selected.

Surfaces and document classes foregrounded, collapsed, hidden, or guarded for that mode.
Workspace Monitor sections that should be available in this mode.
Security interpretation and future enforcement notes.

mode_boundary.view_mode: Audience and UI lens for repository dashboards, document browsers, project monitors, and future desktop surfaces.
mode_boundary.install_mode: Environment setup profile for using or improving the platform.
mode_boundary.work_mode: Task execution and close-out strictness profile such as quick, standard, ship_first, research, or governance.
mode_boundary.rule: Choose view_mode when deciding what to display. Choose install_mode when setting up dependencies. Choose work_mode for each task after web-first intake and memory bootstrap.

modes.label: User View
modes.intent: Show stable project, history, documentation, and generated artifact summaries for someone using or reviewing the platform without improving internals.
audience: reviewer who should not need implementation or governance internals
must_not: Treat a simplified UI lens as security enforcement.
Expose private operational documents in a public snapshot.
Require developer install dependencies just to view user surfaces.
security_notes: Public deployment must filter snapshot data at collection time, not only hide UI sections.
Future authenticated deployments should enforce least privilege outside the client component.

modes.label: Developer View
modes.intent: Show implementation, tests, requirements, specs, agents, and verification surfaces needed by someone improving a project or platform feature.
audience: agent modifying tools, workflows, validators, or dashboards
must_not: Assume developer view can bypass work_mode evaluator gates.
Mix unrelated project internals without boundary notes.
Treat hidden superadmin controls as unavailable to the repository owner.
security_notes: Developer view is for local/private operator use until authentication is implemented.
Future deployment should distinguish developer capabilities from superadmin capabilities.

modes.label: Super Admin Dev
modes.intent: Show the full owner/operator view for building the platform itself, including governance, history, requirements, specs, agents, configs, project boundaries, public-readiness checks, and future admin controls.
audience: agent performing governance or cross-project orchestration work

hide_by_default: local-only folders excluded by collector policy
guard: least privilege design before multi-user deployment

must_not: Publish a superadmin snapshot publicly without redaction review.
Use superadmin convenience as a substitute for explicit access-control design.
Weaken install_mode, work_mode, omission, resource, or evaluation gates.
security_notes: This is the current default because the platform is still under owner-led development.
Before public multi-user use, implement server-side authorization or static snapshot filtering and tests.

selection_rules: Use superadmin_developer by default while the repository is private and the owner is actively building platform governance.
Use developer when the operator improves a project or platform feature but does not need owner-level governance or publication decisions.
Use user when the operator only needs stable outputs, project summaries, and readable history.
Do not confuse view_mode with install_mode or work_mode.
For public deployment, view_mode must be paired with collector-level publication filters before relying on it for privacy.
